subject: Food Science
title: Blanching Vegetables
description: Learn Blanching Vegetables in one minute.

hook.text: Frozen broccoli without blanching turns brown, bitter, and mushy within weeks.

buildup.text: Blanching is brief immersion in boiling water (90–100°C for 1–5 minutes) followed by immediate cooling in ice water.

discovery.text: Blanching inactivates enzymes—polyphenol oxidase, lipoxygenase, and peroxidase.

twist.text: Over-blanching leaches water-soluble vitamins (C and B). Under-blanching leaves enzymes active.

climax.text: Steam blanching retains more nutrients than water blanching because vegetables don't contact water directly.

punchline.text: Three minutes in boiling water, then ice. Enzymes die.

quiz.question: Why is blanching necessary before freezing vegetables?
options: To inactivate enzymes that cause browning, off-flavors, and vitamin loss during frozen storage
